title: Dialogue Options
text:
Cycle through dialogue options with <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. Press <Input actionName="ChoiceApply" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to select one.

<Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Gold dialogue options</> represent important choices that progress the conversation. <Rich color="MainColors.Blue">Blue dialogue options</> represent choices that might reveal valuable information or lead to interesting interactions. Some of them tie into your life path.

Some dialogue options will appear grayed out, meaning you do not meet the Attribute requirement necessary to make that choice.

title: Fast Travel
text:
As you explore Night City, you will come across and unlock Fast Travel Dataterms: <Image id="MappinIcons.FastTravelMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>

Interact with the nearest Dataterm to view a map with all currently unlocked locations. Select one with <Input context="UIShared" actionName="world_map_menu_fast_travel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to travel there.

title: Journal, Phone, Jobs
text:
Your Journal contains information about available, active and completed Jobs as well as their specific objectives. Open the Journal with <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenJournalMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> from the main menu.

You have a minimap in your HUD, but you can also open the full map with <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenMapMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> from the main menu. Use the map to track objectives from active Jobs and other useful leads. It also displays points of interests such as vendors, ripperdoc clinics, fast travel points and available work.

Hold <Input context="UI_DPad" actionName="PhoneInteract" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to access your phone, allowing you to call or message people from your list of contacts. If you want to open a message you just received, press <Input actionName="NotificationOpen" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> or navigate to the Messages tab in the main menu. These messages will often contain useful information about your current Job or Gig.

Night City is a living, breathing world that offers many places to explore. Pay attention to your surroundings and check your map and phone regularly.

GIGS: <Image id="MappinIcons.Gigs" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> These work opportunities are obtained from fixers throughout Night City. When you enter a district, you'll receive a message from the local fixer with a list of available Gigs and they will become marked on your map. When you near a Gig's location, you'll receive a message with additional details. These details will also be stored in your Journal.
NCPD SCANNER HUSTLES: <Image id="MappinIcons.NCPDScanner" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> These are jobs contracted out by the Night City Police Department. That's right – the NCPD is willing to pay mercs for settling public safety issues that they don't have the resources to handle themselves... Or maybe they just don't have the guts.

Note: it will automatically park in the nearest available spot, provided you have street access.

All vehicles you’ve received or purchased are stored in your Garage. To mark a vehicle as active for the Call Vehicle function, access your Garage menu by holding <Input actionName="CallVehicle" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, browse available vehicles with <Input context="UIShared" actionName="navigate_up" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UIShared" actionName="navigate_down" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then press <Input context="UIShared" actionName="proceed" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to select one.

You can hijack occupied vehicles provided you meet the Body Attribute requirement necessary to pull the driver out of the driver's seat. You can steal unoccupied vehicles provided you meet the Technical Ability Attribute requirement.

title: Driving Basics
text:
Navigating Night City can be a challenge. Narrow streets, dense traffic… But don’t sweat it. Here are some tips that will help you get around with any vehicle.

Maintaining Traction

Your tires can only handle so much at once. If you need to turn hard, avoid braking and accelerating hard at the same time. Brake before the corner, then steer smoothly into it. Stay off the brakes and gas mid turn, then accelerate gently as you come out of the corner. This will improve your speed and stability. When your tires start to smoke and squeal, it means you’re either approaching or exceeding the maximum grip they can provide.

Oversteer and Understeer

Ever entered a corner at high speed but it feels like your vehicle won’t turn? That's called understeer. To avoid it, slow down before entering the corner and try not to accelerate or brake mid corner.

Or maybe you’ve tried to turn hard at high speed but the rear of the vehicle whipped around, causing you to spin out of control? This is oversteer. Braking before the turn and careful acceleration mid corner can help prevent it, but you can also steer into the direction of the slide to correct it and regain stability. This is called countersteering.

During an oversteer slide, you can also keep your foot on the gas and apply the right amount of countersteer to enter and maintain a controlled slide. Congrats – now you’re drifting!

Effective Braking

You can brake in two ways: Brakes and the Handbrake. Regular brakes apply to all wheels and are the most effective way to bring you to a stop. If you apply them while stopped, they will put your vehicle in reverse. While in reverse, your input for Brake now accelerates and your input for Accelerate now brakes.

The Handbrake only applies to the rear wheels, so it is not as effective, but you can use it to execute sharp turns and reverse direction quickly if you use it without accelerating. If you want to slide (i.e. drift) through a turn, tap the Handbrake just before turning while continuing to accelerate. With the right countersteering and enough practice, you’ll be able to control your slide through the entire corner.

Keyboard (Digital) vs Controller (Analog)

Some driving techniques require gentle or gradual input for acceleration and braking. Unfortunately, keyboards don’t accommodate gradual input. Controllers are better suited for driving because analog triggers and sticks work best for slow, smooth inputs. Try pressing your Accelerate and Brake inputs gently at first, then gradually apply more pressure to experiment with how acceleration, braking and steering interact. Often just a little is just right.

Maximizing Camera Perspective

Each camera perspective has its own merits. First-Person Perspective (FPP) may improve your sense of immersion, giving you the impression you’re really behind the wheel. Third-Person Perspective (TPP), by contrast, improves visibility and awareness of your surroundings. But no matter which perspective you use, you can still manually rotate the camera and reset it with a single button press.

TPP has three camera distances you can select in game and two camera heights you can select from in the Settings. The camera system is intentionally designed to require more player input to get the best view of the action. It’s worth practicing and experimenting with camera control so you can learn to position it to see where you’re going before you get there.

title: Choosing a Vehicle
text:
In Night City, every ride has its own charm, character and performance. Pick the one that suits your style, packs enough punch to be fun, and has handling characteristics that feel natural to you!

That said, vehicles that share the same engine placement and drive-wheel configuration will also share similar handling traits. There are three drive-wheel configurations: front, rear and all-wheel. Each has unique traction behavior under different circumstances. There are also three engine placements: front, mid and rear. This affects a vehicle's center of mass and thus its handling. Don’t know what a given ride has? Scan it! But if there’s any doubt, you can always pop the trunk or hood to see for yourself.

Front-Wheel Drive, Front Engine

These vehicles are typically the easiest to drive with good traction on slippery surfaces, and predictable understeer when pushed too hard. Engaging Burn Out mode mid-turn will produce a milder slide than with other configurations.

Rear-Wheel Drive, Front Engine

A classic combination for luxury, sport and muscle cars, designed for drivers with above-average skill. This configuration provides near-even weight balance with the engine at the front and passengers and drive axle towards the rear. Handling is generally neutral, producing only mild oversteer, but heavy gas mid corner can kick the rear out, allowing for drifting and quick changes of direction.

All-Wheel Drive, Front Engine

An excellent choice for medium-skill drivers who like to move fast whether in the city or off road. Considered the most stable configuration, you can brake or accelerate in the middle of a turn much more than in others, allowing for both beautiful slides as well as incredible traction and speed when exiting corners.

Rear-Wheel Drive, Mid or Rear Engine

A configuration for only the most skilled gearheads. With most of the weight behind the driver, these vehicles can understeer under acceleration when turning, and can spin if you Accelerate or Brake too suddenly mid corner. To keep these vehicles in one piece, it requires slow and smooth inputs. But if you’ve got the skill, they can provide a unique and rewarding thrill ride… if you like livin’ on the edge.

All-Wheel Drive, Mid or Rear Engine

This combination gives the feel of a RWD mid engine, but with the traction of AWD, and is favored by powerful, high-end exotics. Driven gingerly, they benefit from stable handling with mild understeer, but they can put down power like no other configuration and change direction easily. If you notice too much understeer, just feed it more gas. Put the pedal to the metal coming out of a corner, and they’ll have you flyin’ down the road like a bat outta hell!

title: Burn Out Mode
text:
A “burn out” occurs when the drive wheels spin faster than the vehicle is moving, causing the tires to melt and smoke, but Burn Out Mode can do so much more. Try engaging it at medium and lower speeds and applying different levels of input. To get the most out of Burn Out Mode, we recommend driving with a controller rather than a keyboard. Analog triggers and sticks allow you to gradually or partially apply the brake and gas, which is crucial for some of these maneuvers.

To engage Burn Out Mode, press and hold Brake and Accelerate simultaneously either while stopped or moving at lower speeds. Your drive wheels will start to burn out, while the opposite wheels brake, keeping the vehicle mostly in place (technically, this is a Brake Stand).

Turning Around in Tight Spaces

Car stuck in a narrow, dead-end alleyway? Engage Burn Out Mode and begin steering to rotate your vehicle on the spot!

Tire Temperature and High-Grip Boost

Spinning your tires builds heat, and heat improves their traction. Once you’ve got your tires good ‘n’ hot, release the brake to launch your vehicle with a drag-race-like High-Grip Boost. Note: Tire temperature only affects the grip of the tires during launch.

Stunting, Drifting, Donuts, Rolling Brake Stands and More!

With Burn Out Mode engaged from a stop, slowly release the brake to perform a rolling brake stand. You can steer at the same time to rotate the vehicle and smoke the tires.

To drift, you can either apply the Handbrake during a turn or by engaging Burn Out Mode when entering a corner at lower speeds. Practice enough and you can pull off donuts, learn to drift in a circle or just quickly change direction. You could even trigger a High-Grip Boost then and take off like a shot. This mode isn’t just for fun – it can also bail you out when things get hot and you need a slick getaway!

Front-Wheel Drive Vehicles

Burn Out Mode can be engaged with this vehicle type, but the ability to perform some maneuvers is limited compared to vehicles with other drivetrain configurations.

All-Wheel Drive Vehicles

These vehicles use on-board computers that determine how much power goes to the front or rear wheels. When Burn Out Mode is engaged, the computers kill power to the front wheels, causing the vehicle to behave as if it’s rear-wheel drive. The same effect happens when a Handbrake is used.

Heavy-Duty Vehicles

Burn Out Mode can technically be activated for any vehicle, but some of the largest, slowest vehicles can never get their wheels spinning fast enough to have any real effect.

Keyboard Limitations – WASD and Arrow Key Bindings

If you are using a keyboard to drive (again, a controller is recommended), please note that many keyboards do not register more than 2 keys pressed at the same time if located near each other. For example, if you engage Burn Out Mode by holding the W and S keys, the A and D keys may not work. This is why we have the arrow keys simultaneously bound for driving controls. You can work around the aforementioned problem by activating Burn Out Mode with the W and S keys and using the left and right arrow keys to steer.

title: Advanced Techniques
text:
So, think you’ve got the basics down? Then it’s time for a few pro tips. 

Pay Attention to Your Tires

If you push your tires to the limit, they’ll start to squeal and smoke. Take this as a warning sign you’re about to lose traction. If you notice the front wheels squealing first or more than in the rear, this means the vehicle will experience understeer if you continue to push it. If the rear tires are squealing more, then expect oversteer instead. Recognizing these signs early may mean you’ll have time to counter the effect. If your main objective is pure speed, try not to smoke your tires as that creates too much friction, which slows you down, and adds resistance to your engine.

Listen for Chassis Impacts

Night City has many drivable surfaces, everything from smooth roads to bumpy roads to fully off road. Some vehicles are more suited for a given road surface because of their suspension type and ground clearance. If you’re going over bumpy desert terrain in a low-clearance exotic car, for example, you may hear crash-like sounds, notice the vehicle bouncing and find it difficult to control. This is because the bottom of the car is hitting the ground.

The Handbrake: Emergency Braking vs Drifting

The Handbrake is a versatile tool depending on what you use it for. Of course, pressing it while not accelerating will lock the rear tires and bring you to a halt. You can also turn at the last moment for a sharp turn or spin. But if you continue to accelerate while using the Handbrake, it acts more like a drift button, halving the brake power and creating a smoother slide. You can continue to hold it for as long as you like, but typically a quick tap to initiate a slide is enough for a simple drift.

Free Rev with Grip Boost – Forward and Reverse

From Burn Out Mode you can only launch forward. However, you can still perform a High-Grip Boost from a standstill in both forward AND reverse if you launch while using Free Rev and your tires haven’t cooled yet. To Free Rev, hold Accelerate or Brake while holding Handbrake to make your engine rev up, then release just the Handbrake to launch. If you’re holding Brake, you’ll perform a High-Grip Boost in reverse!

J-Turns (AKA Rockfords)

A J-Turn is a driving maneuver that allows you to drive in reverse, then quickly rotate the vehicle 180 degrees and continue driving in the same direction but now facing forward. It can also be performed from forward to reverse. To go from reverse to forward, go as fast as possible in reverse with Brake, turn sharply to face the direction in which you are already moving, then press Accelerate. Going from forward to reverse works in a similar way, although you will need to use the Handbrake to perform the sharp 180-degree turn. The vehicle’s computer will know if you are attempting a J-Turn and will do a super quick flat-shift from reverse to first gear (or vice versa) once the turn is complete.

Maximizing Burn Out Mode

We encourage you to experiment with Burn Out Mode at different speeds and to combine different maneuvers. One example: Use the Handbrake to start an aggressive slide, then engage Burn Out Mode by simultaneously pressing Accelerate and Brake at lower speeds, slide to face any direction, and release the Brake to launch with a High-Grip Boost.

Another example: Say you’re moving in reverse then decide to go forward. Ordinarily, you would stop pressing Brake and start pressing Accelerate, which would slow the car to a complete stop and then smoothly shift from reverse to first gear. Instead, you can engage Burn Out Mode, which immediately flat shifts the vehicle into first gear, smokes the tires and provides immediate forward thrust.

Remember – Burn Out Mode also works on bikes, but with a couple preem differences. A High-Grip Boost on a bike can trigger wheelies, and the much increased grip you get off the line can be used to do things and get places that aren’t possible in other vehicles!

title: Grappling and Takedowns
text:
You can grapple enemies who haven't detected you by pressing <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

You can still move while grappling an enemy, and can choose to perform a lethal <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> or non-lethal <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> Takedown.

The enemy will struggle to free themselves from your grip. If you hold them too long, they will eventually break free. High-level enemies, marked with a <Image id="UIIcon.q000_tutorial_icon_boss" align="bottom" width="70" height="70"></>, will break free more quickly.

Although some high-level enemies cannot be grappled, you can still perform Takedowns on them while undetected. Using certain abilities and items, as well as cleverly using the environment to your advantage, will help you remain out of sight. Some bosses might require multiple Takedowns to defeat.

Enemies and security systems may notice and react to bodies you leave out in the open. Make sure to dump the bodies in appropriate hiding locations (a dumpster, for example) or otherwise in areas that are not easily visible to enemies.

Hold <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> to pick up a body, then press <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to dump it.

To dump a body in an appropriate container, approach it while holding the body and press <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. If you perform a Takedown on an enemy directly next to one of these containers, you will hide the body there automatically.

Remember: these containers have limited capacity, and once you've placed a body in one it cannot be removed.

All loot from dumped bodies is automatically dropped to the ground in front of the container.

title: Combat and Alerted State
text:
An enemy is in a Combat State if it is actively attacking its target or approaching its last known location.

When an enemy cannot locate its target, it will fall back to an Alerted State and begin patrolling the area to search for the threat, making it more difficult to sneak around them. If an enemy finds a body, they will remain in a permanent Alerted State.

title: Patrols and Distraction
text:
Enemies patrolling an area follow a pattern that can be observed and used to your advantage.

Some devices allow you to distract enemies and divert them from their path. An enemy who is distracted will have a white outline.

Noises such as human footsteps or silenced gunshots can also alert an enemy, who will then try to locate the source. Louder noises such as a combat-initiating shout or a dying shout will make enemies enter an Alerted State or enter directly into combat.

title: Cyberdeck
text:
Cyberdecks unlock Netrunner abilities that allow the user to quickhack people and devices.

Each cyberdeck comes with a base set of pre-installed quickhacks, a limited number of slots for equipped quickhacks and a certain amount of RAM which is required to execute them. Different cyberdeck models can vary in terms of their stats and power. Higher Tier decks are able to perform more advanced quickhacks.

You can access your cyberdeck in the Inventory or Cyberware screens through the main menu <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenHubMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Cyberdeck RAM
text:
RAM is a resource used when performing quickhacks. When you upload a quickhack to an enemy or device, it uses up a certain amount of RAM units. A quickhack's RAM cost can be altered in different ways, such as certain cyberware abilities, Perks and differences in level. RAM recovers automatically over time.

Your maximum RAM can be increased with a higher Intelligence Attribute, certain cyberware abilities and Perks as well as by equipping a better cyberdeck.

title: Device Quickhacks
text:
Every cyberdeck comes with a pre-installed set of quickhacks. You can find specific details about them and about the cyberdeck in their descriptions.

To upload quickhacks, you must have enough RAM available on your cyberdeck. RAM cost can be altered by different means, such as your level, specific Perks or cyberware abilities.

To upload a quickhack, activate your scanner with <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, aim at the device, select a quickhack from the list using <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then press <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_ApplyAndClose" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to execute it.

Distract Enemies <Image id="UIIcon.Malfunction" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Causes a device to malfunction, resulting in erratic behavior that will distract nearby people.

Remote Deactivation <Image id="UIIcon.ToggleState" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Manipulates basic device functions, such as opening/closing doors and activating/deactivating cameras.

Camera Control <Image id="UIIcon.TakeControl" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Grants full remote control of the camera.

Initiate Overload <Image id="UIIcon.OverLoadDevice" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Overloads a device's electrical circuitry, permanently destroying it.

Friendly Mode <Image id="UIIcon.OverrideAttitude" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Overrides the target's recognition module, causing you to be perceived as an ally and authorization holder. Turrets and cameras treat your enemies as their enemies and assist in combat whether you are in combat or undetected.

Assist Mode <Image id="UIIcon.SetDeviceTagKillMode" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Forces a turret's targeting into manual mode.

Take Control <Image id="UIIcon.TakeControl" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Enables remote operation of turrets and computers.

title: Antipersonnel Quickhacks
text:
Cyberdecks have special slots reserved for antipersonnel quickhacks to use against your enemies, and can be customized to suit your playstyle.

Open your Inventory and click on the Cyberdeck slot to change which quickhacks you have actively installed.

To upload a quickhack into a target, you must have enough RAM available on your cyberdeck. RAM cost can be altered by different means, such as specific Perks and cyberware abilities.

To upload a quickhack, activate your scanner with <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, aim at your target, select a quickhack from the list using <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then press <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_ApplyAndClose" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to execute it.

New quickhacks can be found throughout the world, purchased from vendors, earned as rewards, and sometimes acquired from uploading the Datamine daemon to network Access Points. You can also craft them if you possess the necessary Crafting Specs. Quickhack Crafting Specs can found throughout the world, purchased from vendors, and earned as rewards.

title: Access Points
text:
Access Points are physical ports through which it is possible to access the local network. They can be found by exploring your surroundings or by performing the Ping quickhack on a device or person connected to the same network.

Successfully uploading a Datamine daemon into an Access Point can grant you money, quickhack crafting specs or components, and sometimes even an entirely new quickhack.

title: Health, Regeneration and Armor
text:
Health is a measure of your vitality. Your Max Health increases when you level up. It can be increased further by investing in your Body Attribute as well as in certain Perks and cyberware.

Outside of combat, your Health will fully regenerate automatically. It regenerates even faster when you consume food.

During combat, Health regeneration is not available by default. You can unlock this ability by acquiring the Painkiller Perk, which can be found in the Body Attribute's Perk tree. Taking a shower in V's apartment will also temporarily give you this ability.

Armor reduces the amount of damage you take from direct hits. As you progress, your enemies will gain access to more powerful weapons. Increasing your Armor will improve your chances of survival. Cyberware is the primary source of Armor, but some Perks and clothing items can help reduce the damage you take in other ways.

title: Stamina
text:
Stamina is a measure of your endurance. Certain movements that can give you an edge in combat, such dodging and sprinting, require Stamina to perform.

You can improve how quickly your Stamina is drained and how quickly it regenerates by investing in certain Perks and Cyberware.

Movement, shooting and melee attacks all use Stamina. Your Stamina will begin to regenerate automatically after a short time, but how quickly it begins and how long it lasts depends on the type of weapon you have equipped.

The lower your Stamina, the more your proficiency and accuracy with ranged weapons will suffer. Likewise, at low Stamina, your melee attacks will be slower and deal reduced damage.

title: Leveling Up
text:
Completing jobs and other activities will give experience points (XP) that increase your level.

Every level you gain, you earn an Attribute Point and Perk Point that can be spent to unlock a Perk within a Perk tree.

You can level up a Skill by performing actions related to that Skill. After all, practice makes perfect!

title: Attributes and Perks
text:
Attributes represent the possible range of your abilities as a mercenary. They can be improved by investing the Attribute Points you earn from leveling up.

Each Attribute also contains a Perk tree. Perks offer unique abilities and boosts to your gameplay experience. They can be unlocked by investing the Perk Points you earn from leveling up. These points can be refunded, so feel free to experiment!

By improving an Attribute, you receive a variety of bonuses:

BODY determines your raw physical power and fortitude. It improves your proficiency with Shotguns, Light Machine Guns and Blunt Weapons. It also enables you to open some doors by force, rip off turrets, and use intimidating or solo-trained dialogue choices. +2 Max Health per Attribute Point.

COOL determines your assassination skills and stealth abilities. It improves your proficiency with Precision Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Handguns and Throwable Weapons. It also enables you to use advanced, stealthy Perk abilities and subtle or street-smart dialogue choices. +1.25% Crit Damage per Attribute Point.

INTELLIGENCE determines your netrunning abilities. It improves your proficiency with Smart Weapons and allows you to unleash your full potential as a netrunner. It also enables you to access local subnets and show off your knowledge of the Net in dialogues. +1 Max RAM per 4 Attribute Points.

REFLEXES determine your maneuverability and ability to evade enemy attacks. It improves your proficiency with Assault Rifles, Submachine Guns and Blades, and enables you to use advanced movements. It also enables you to make quick, observant remarks in dialogues. +0.5% Crit Chance per Attribute Point.

TECHNICAL ABILITY determines your techie know-how. It improves your proficiency with explosives and Tech Weapons and allows you to be compatible with high-end cyberware. It also allows you to bypass some locks, override devices and exhibit tech-savvy knowledge in dialogues. +2 Armor per Attribute Point.

title: Skills
text: Skills represent your proficiency in various gameplay elements and can be improved by performing related actions. As you improve them, you'll unlock thematic bonuses.

title: Street Cred
text:
Street Cred is the measure of your reputation in Night City. As your Street Cred grows, you will gain access to new vehicle offers and vendor discounts beyond the reach of small-time punks.

Night City is bursting with opportunity, so get out there and make a name for yourself!

title: Weapons
text:
Ranged weapons are grouped by manufacturer and technology type.

Power weapons, when coupled with Ballistics Coprocessor cyberware, allow you to control your bullets' ricochet trajectory.

Tech weapons allow you to charge shots that can penetrate cover and walls to hit enemies.

Smart weapons, when coupled with Smart Link cyberware, allow you to lock onto targets and fire homing rounds.

Ammo is shared between all weapons that belong to the same category:
- Handgun Ammo (Pistols, Revolvers, SMGs)
- Heavy Ammo (Assault Rifles, Precision Rifles, LMGs)
- Shotgun Ammo (Shotguns)
- Sniper Ammo (Sniper Rifles)

Ranged weapons can be improved with attachments such as sights, scopes and muzzle brakes. Their stats can also be improved by installing mods. You can see available mod slots by selecting a weapon from your inventory. Melee weapons, which are categorized into Blades and Blunt Weapons, can similarly be modded.

Weapons can also be crafted and upgraded from the main menu:  <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenHubMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Combat Gadgets
text:
The Combat Gadget quickslot allows for quick use of grenades and certain combat cyberware.

Press <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to use.
Hold <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> for precise aiming.

To assign an item, hold <Input actionName="WeaponWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quick-access menu, go to the Combat Gadget quickslot with <Input actionName="UI_TutorFakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, cycle through available items with <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_PreviousAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_NextAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then select one to equip.

Combat gadgets can also be assigned in your inventory by selecting the Combat Gadget quickslot.

Grenades do not disappear from your inventory when you use them. Instead, they use charges, which recharge automatically over time. The number of charges, the recharge rate, and other grenade effects can be upgraded with certain Perks.

When you acquire a higher Tier of a grenade type you already possess, it will automatically replace the lower Tier version in your inventory. You cannot possess multiple Tiers for the same grenade at one time.

title: Consumables
text:
The Consumable quickslot allows you to quickly and conveniently use Health Items. Press <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseConsumable" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to use the item assigned to it.

To assign an item, hold <Input actionName="WeaponWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quick-access menu, go to the Consumable quickslot with <Input actionName="UI_TutorFakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, cycle through available items with <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_PreviousAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_NextAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then select one to equip.

Consumables can also be assigned in your Inventory by selecting the Consumable quickslot.

Food, drinks and boosters can only be consumed from the Inventory. To do so, hover over an item and hold <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="use_item" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

Health Items, such as inhalers and injectors, do not disappear from your inventory when you use them. Instead, they use charges which recharge automatically over time. The number of charges, recharge rate, and other effects can be upgraded with certain Perks and Cyberware.

When you acquire a higher Tier of a Health Item you already possess, it will automatically replace the lower Tier version in your inventory. You cannot possess multiple Tiers for the same Health Item at one time.

Food regenerates Health. Drinks regenerate Stamina.

Effects gained from consumables do not stack. A new effect will replace the current one.

title: Crafting and Upgrading
text:
You can craft and upgrade items from the Crafting tab of the main menu.

To craft an item, you'll need the Crafting Spec for it as well as the necessary components.

Crafting Specs can be purchased at vendors or found in loot. A Crafting Spec's color indicates the Tier of the item you're crafting. You can craft weapons, weapon mods and attachments, quickhacks, consumable items, combat gadgets, ammo and even other crafting components.

You start the game with a set <Rich color="RarityColor.Common">Tier 1</> and <Rich color="RarityColor.Uncommon">Tier 2</> Crafting Specs for weapons and weapon attachments as well as all Crafting Specs for ammo and components.

Crafted weapons have fixed stats and a fixed number of mod slots.

Whenever you acquire an Iconic weapon, you can immediately upgrade it to next Tier, provided you have the necessary components. Upgrading a weapon increases its stats. Iconic weapons cannot be upgraded after reaching the highest Tier.

title: Status Effects
text:
Weapons, quickhacks, daemons and some devices can inflict various long-term status effects on both you and your enemies. The duration of status effects on enemies is displayed by their name.

Bleeding <Image id="UIIcon.wounded_disabled_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- slowly depletes Health, disables sprinting and reduces jump height

Blinding <Image id="UIIcon.blinded_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly reduces threat detection and hinders movement

Burn <Image id="UIIcon.burning_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- continuously depletes Health

Crippled <Image id="UIIcon.crippled_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- severely limits combat or movement effectiveness depending on which limb is crippled

EMP <Image id="UIIcon.EMP" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly deactivates or severely limits the combat effectiveness of mechs, drones and robots, in addition to dealing damage

Knockdown <Image id="UIIcon.knockdown_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly knocks to the ground, revealing Weakspots

Poison <Image id="UIIcon.poisoned" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- slowly depletes Health, reduces Armor and slows movement

Stun <Image id="UIIcon.stun_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly immobilizes, leaving vulnerable to attack

title: Encrypted Shards
text:
You can read collected shards by pressing <Input actionName="NotificationOpen" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> when the notification appears. They can also be found in the Shards section of your Journal.

Some shards you find may contain data hidden behind encryption, preventing access from the authorities or nosy edgerunners. Select the CRACK SECURITY option to begin decryption through Breach Protocol and upload the Security Breach daemon in order to access the hidden content.

title: Regina Jones
subtitle: Regina Jones
text: A fixer with Chinese heritage operating out of Watson. She used to work as an independent reporter for FTF Radio, but after the station was acquired by the media conglomerate News 54, Regina decided it was time to find a better medium to spread her message. She mobilized all her contacts – from the highest-ranking corpos to the lowliest dealers, gangers, mercs, bums and junkies. From their point of view, Regina hasn't changed a bit – she's always been a fighter, a girl from the streets. The only difference is that before she bought gossip and sold news – now she spins both.

title: Dino Dinovic
text:
Everyone who's anyone knows him, whether it's Dino the fixer in Downtown and Corpo Plaza, or Dino the rockerboy bassist in the notorious band Gloryhole Bandits. Strangely, despite them playing sold-out shows, nobody's heard Dino play.

You holler at Dino when you need something – pure, uncut stimulants, fast loans, joytoys for your BFF's birthday party, you want to start a riot or want to see somebody's legs broken. Dino's your man – Dino'll get it done.

Like every good fixer, Dino keeps mixed company – he's just at home with play-hard corpos and top-tier mercs (usually edgerunners) as with sketchy media vultures and homeless drifters. You can meet them all in Dino's bar. It's worth dropping in – someone's bound to pick your brain over a drink... or throw up on your shoes. You might leave with a black eye or an STI, but that's how this city rolls?

title: Muamar “El Capitan” Reyes
text:
Before he became a well-known fixer in Santo Domingo, El Capitan was Muamar Reyes – a corpo rat at a company that dealt in... ah who the hell cares anyway. But, all too quickly he realized that with corps it's always the same ol' tune – either they fuck you, or you fuck them. He preferred the latter.

Often those who escape poverty like to help out their less fortunate peers – like El Capitan. Well, kinda. He makes a fortune as the go-to fixer for half of Santo Domingo's working class, but hey – at least he makes sure they can still afford their rent too. Don't like his style? Find your own gigs. But when a gangoon decides they'd rather save a buck by breaking your legs instead of paying your cut, look around – might just see El Capitan watching from his limo window with a smirk on his face.

title: Wakako Okada
text:
If you're looking for decent-paying gigs in Westbrook, go to the pachinko parlor on Jig-Jig Street run by a fixer named Wakako Okada. Rumors abound, but as of yet nobody's worked up the nerve to ask her about her past and her very many, very dead husbands. She didn't kill any of them, probably, but hey, what's important is that they're gone and she's still going strong, growing richer and more powerful by the day.

Every serious player in Night City respects Wakako. Going into a meeting with her is like getting into a cage with a lioness. Sure, the lioness is polite, but you can tell she's already thinking about her next snack. Maybe that's why Wakako's gigs are carried out almost immediately and flawlessly. Wakako takes this entirely for granted.

title: Dakota Smith
text: The Badlands' resident fixer and a member of the Northern Californian Pomo tribe. At first glance Dakota seems like a harmless desert-dweller. It wouldn't be wrong to say that sometime after the Unification War, she lost touch with reality – in her free time she deciphers the secret language of smoke. But if you ignore that, she's an extremely perceptive fixer with a mind for biz few in this part of California wouldn't envy. Those who take on her jobs always make sure they're done to a tee – because firstly, Dakota's never gone behind anyone's back, and secondly if they decided to go behind hers, they'd be vulture breakfast in no time. You'll also notice she doesn't go anywhere without her oxygen tank – she's been huffing pure oxygen for a few decades now.

title: Padre
text:
Real name – Sebastian Ibarra. Formerly a priest in the Valentinos, but after the bloodbath in Moto Cielo he converted to a more noble calling – that of the fixer. He started out by lining up jobs exclusively for his people from Heywood and the Valentinos – later he even shook hands with the likes of 6th Street. Who knows, maybe it's because he softened up in his old age, or maybe it's because all gangs are equal in the eyes of God.

Padre does things according to his own code of honor. He doesn't support any particular group or gang – his interests lie in maintaining the delicate balance of power in Night City.

title: Mr. Hands
subtitle: Mr. Hands
text:
When he was still Wade Bleecker the Petrochem employee, practically everyone knew him. Since scrubbing his identity from existence and adopting the persona of Mr. Hands, Pacifica's resident fixer, that's no longer the case. His appearance and true identity are a closely guarded secret.

In his previous life, Wade climbed fairly high up the Petrochem corporate ladder. But after a sudden shake-up in upper management, someone decided blood needed spilling at the altar of corporate efficiency. Unfortunately for Bleecker, he was chosen as its unfortunate sacrificial lamb. He proved cunning enough to survive the initial assassination attempt, but when an official bounty was put on his head, he had no choice but to change his name and face and disappear for good.

Mr. Hands is a businessman through and through – cool-headed, calculating and supremely focused on his objective. Precisely what that objective is, however, remains a mystery to all but Mr. Hands himself.

title: Jotaro Shobo
text: If Night City had a contest for the most rotten-to-the-core piece of human garbage, Jotaro Shobo would stand a pretty decent chance of winning. Maybe not first place, but he'd definitely be up there. Jotaro is a high-ranking Tyger Claws ganger who, thanks to his intelligence, loyalty and ruthlessness, quickly made his way up the pecking order. He rules his lackeys with an iron fist and is never late with his cut for the bosses, who repay him with protection and turning a blind eye to his various "hobbies." One of them includes recording braindances, and anyone who's relived them calls him the devil of Kabuki.

title: Mikhail Akulov
text: Officially, the Soviet fixer is on a diplomatic business trip in Night City, but most take that explanation with a heap of salt. Unofficially, one rumor has it that Akulov has been seduced by Night City's capitalist, libertine charms. Still, the million eurodollar question remains – what is he really doing here? Many would pay handsomely for the answer. After all, this is a man who represents the interests of the entire USSR.

title: Tiny Mike
text: Tiny Mike was one of countless kids raised by the streets of Night City. Crafty, streetwise and familiar with all the people worth knowing. But one detail separates him from most of the pack – he's still alive. These days he's merc who began his career with a fast start. At 11, he stood watch for the Tyger Claws. At 12, they had him dealing. Then three years later he set off to make a name for himself. It didn't take Tiny long to realize only two things really matter on the streets: sticking to your word and cold, hard cash (not necessarily in that order). Dozens of scars and close calls later, he finally achieved what he always wanted: recognition. Fixers knew his name and kept the jobs and eddies flowing his way. He often worked with his brother, Big Pete, though Tiny would tell you it was usually "too often." After all, mixing family and work can be risky biz – a rare stance that corpos and street urchins alike can agree on.

title: Gottfrid Persson
text: Gottfrid's work is the stuff of another person's nightmares. Nightmares often come true in Night City, and when they do, he takes them (or buys them) and edits them to turn a profit. As a matter of fact, he's fairly well-respected in the obscure circle of illegal braindance editors. He's a craftsman without a conscience - an advantage in his line of work. If the material is good, Gottfrid will take a raw BD from anyone and fine-tune the emotions, no questions asked. The closest person to him is his son, Fredrik, whom he taught and trained in his craft. When they're not editing together, they manage a deep net site.

title: Fredrik Persson
text: Throughout their lives, many a man has struggled to break free from their father's shadow. But not Fredrik. The shadows suit him just fine. He has everything he needs - money and emotional fulfillment. Gottfrid is professional and knowledgeable, while Fredrik is passionate and uncompromising. Together they form a duo that Night City happens to need. After all, someone has to edit all those illegal braindances.

title: Iris Tanner
text:
Iris Tanner is a talented techie and the textbook example of someone whose job is their life. When it comes to a gig, it's never about the money , but the challenge. Still, that doesn't stop her from being a tough negotiator – it's the only way to be taken seriously.

Despite being terse and hard to talk to, she's convinced she's good at reading people – what she doesn't realize is that her deep-seated desire to be admired for her skills actually makes her easy to manipulate. That's one of the reasons she got into serious trouble with the Raffen Shiv.

On principle, Iris doesn't work with fixers, but she's willing to make an exception for Dakota – not because she likes her, but because this time she needs her.

title: Gustavo Orta
text: Open an encyclopedia and flip to the "Valentinos." You should find a picture of Gustavo Orta – or more likely his mugshot. But who reads encyclopedias these days anyway? Just one look at Gustavo Orta and you know he's a Valentino inside and out. His style could be characterized as ruthless – a trait that's certainly helped him climb to the peak of the gang's ranks. Recently, however, Gustavo has been acting... strangely. If the rumors are true, he spends more time silently contemplating the water in the bay than doing what he's been known and feared for – brutally stamping out his rivals in Heywood.

title: Corporal Hare
text: When 17-year-old William Hare first saw a poster promoting service in Militech's paramilitary forces, he finally understood his purpose in life. As his impressionable eyes scanned the multi-million-dollar equipment and armored soldiers, he felt a brutal power and desire for adventure swell inside him. How could a kid who spent his whole life in the slums of Rancho Coronado resist? The promotional specialists in Militech's recruitment office certainly think so, and they're usually right. Hare enlisted and eventually rose to the rank of Corporal. He got everything he dreamed of plus more – combat military-grade cyberware, a sense of power, camaraderie and adventure. As for the latter, there are some parts he'd rather forget – especially the ones he's forbidden to talk about. After Brazil, everything changed. He lost his good health and came back to Night City a veteran, but with no hope of ever returning to active duty.  That's when Hare first asked himself – had Militech taken away more than they gave him?

title: Bartolomeo Mordellini
text: Bartolomeo owns a yacht that has never set sail or left the marina. No surprise there – the water in the bay's toxic, riddled with mines from the war and tangled in strong currents. So why have a yacht? Well, for parties, obviously. The crème de la Night City crème gather on the deck to relax and forget about all their really important life problems. Bartolomeo mingles among them, laughs, pours Champaradise and cuts the good stuff on a silver platter. Then when everyone's loosey goosey and itching for action, he starts scrolling. Bartolomeo's recordings are low quality, chaotic and edited without any rhyme or reason, but they still fetch a handsome price on the black market.

title: Jack Mausser
text: Jack's a merc, or rather – was. He enjoyed his work just a little too much and became an adrenaline junkie. Where clients want discretion, Jack wants to hear screams. So one day, instead of taking out his target quietly, he put on a show for the entire city. Fair enough – it was only a matter of time before Jack pissed someone off and landed in their crosshairs. So what did he do? He quickly bought a run-down club in City Center, fenced it in with guards and shacked up in the VIP area. He knows it's not enough to save his skin, but at least it'll make his assassin's life just a teensy bit harder.

title: Flavio dos Santos
text: Some people are luckier than they deserve to be. No matter what they do, they always land on all fours without a scratch. Sooner or later they start thinking they're invincible, and that's when they become dangerous – to themselves and everyone around them. Nobody fits that description better than Flavio. Chatty and grinning a Cheshire grin, he thinks he can do whatever he wants. Better to steer clear of people like him, unless, of course, someone pays you to help him out.

title: V (Streetkid)
text: They say if you wanna understand the streets, you gotta live 'em. Gangs, fixers, dolls, small-time pushers – you were raised by them all. Down here the law of the jungle dictates the weak serve the strong – the only law in Night City you have yet to break.

title: V (Nomad)
text: Roaming the Badlands, looting scrapyards, raiding fuel depots – life on the road wasn't easy. But growing up in a nomad clan has its perks. Honesty, integrity, and a love of freedom – qualities that few in Night City possess, and no amount of money can buy.

title: V (Corpo)
subtitle: V (Corpo)
text: Few leave the corporate world with their lives – fewer still with their souls intact. You've been there – you've bent the rules, exploited secrets and weaponized information. There's no such thing as a fair game, only winners and losers.

title: Jackie Welles
subtitle: Jackie Welles
text:
A proud son of Heywood and an even prouder son of Mama Welles. Jackie's stubborn – when he wants something, he won't stop (or shut up about it) until he gets his hands on it. Jackie always wanted a lot out of life – maybe too much.

As a teenager, he joined the Valentinos gang, but realizing how much he was capable of – he quit. For years he hustled through the unforgiving world of mercwork, because you need more than a go-getter attitude to sit at the big boys' table – you need street cred. Jackie's life goal has always been to become a legend at the Afterlife and make a heap of eddies along the way.

text:
If you're looking for decent-paying gigs in Westbrook, go to the pachinko parlor on Jig-Jig Street run by a fixer named Wakako Okada.
